prompt: A PVC is Bound and VolumeAttachment is attached, but the Pod reports FailedMount. Diagnose safely.
directAnswer: Bind cluster, Pod/PVC/PV UIDs, volumeHandle, node and driver version. Bound proves claim/PV identity; attached proves controller attachment to a node. Inspect Pod events and CSI node stage/publish operations, device/filesystem state, mount options, credentials and Pod security context. Do not reprovision or force detach. Repair the node/driver/filesystem/permission owner, then verify mount identity/capacity, bounded write-read-cleanup and application operation.
foundation: Binding, attachment, mounting and application I/O are separate stages.
reasoningSteps: Inspect node CSI operations and Pod events.
seniorAnswer: I start after successful controller attachment and preserve operation IDs. I diagnose node staging/publishing through filesystem and security context, avoid destructive detach/recreate, and close only after application-level verification.
weakAnswer: Delete the PVC and recreate the Pod.
whyWeak: It risks data destruction and ignores the proven stage boundary.

followUps.answer: It weakens security without proving driver, mount or identity cause.
Prove fencing and attachment ownership before any force.
Only disposable test file/object after handle/finalizer review.
